strings.name: Witi Ihimaera
strings.summary: Ihimaera pioneered Māori short-story collections and novels, connecting family, land, myth and contemporary identity with international readers. The Whale Rider later became a film. He also worked in diplomacy and teaching; in 2009 he apologized for unacknowledged passages in a novel. Recent work returns to Māori-language learning and the world of The Whale Rider.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Brings Māori literature into international reading and film through works such as The Whale Rider, widening public expression of Indigenous stories.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Gisborne, New Zealand; grew up among Māori communities and on a farm.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied part time at Victoria University of Wellington, completing a BA in 1971.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Māori stories across borders
strings.highlights.h1.text: The Whale Rider joins ancestral inheritance and a girl's development; its 2002 film adaptation widened its audience.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Returning to language
strings.highlights.h2.text: Te Kaikaukau / The Swimmer records returning to immersive Māori-language study at eighty.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Published The Star Path
strings.timeline.t1.text: The young-adult novel returns to The Whale Rider's world, exploring belonging through Pacific and Antarctic voyages.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Published a language-learning memoir
strings.timeline.t2.text: Te Kaikaukau / The Swimmer connects learning, shame, family and cultural reclamation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Apologized over plagiarism
strings.timeline.t3.text: Acknowledged unattributed passages in The Trowenna Sea as negligent and said he would buy remaining warehouse copies.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published Nights in the Gardens of Spain
strings.timeline.t4.text: The novel explored gay identity, family relationships and social expectations.
strings.timeline.t5.title: The Whale Rider appeared
strings.timeline.t5.text: A Māori girl's connection with whales reworked relationships between leadership, gender and tradition.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Published his first novel, Tangi
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became the first Māori novelist in print; also joined the foreign ministry that year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Published his first story collection
strings.timeline.t7.text: Pounamu Pounamu brought contemporary Māori life into New Zealand literature.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed his university degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a BA while balancing employment and part-time study, before developing his publishing career.
